newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-VAN GAAL PROMISES SWEEPING CHANGES AT BARCELONA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VAN GAAL PROMISES SWEEPING CHANGES AT BARCELONA.

text.p: Barcelona presented Louis van Gaal as new coach on Monday, and with him the sweeping organisational changes which the former Ajax manager will bring to one of Europe's biggest clubs.
"I've asked Barcelona to use a new structure," said van Gaal, who will work alongside predecessor as coach Bobby Robson in the new system.
Robson, who still has a year left on his two-year contract, will stay on to superintend new signings.
A further, as yet unnamed man, will manage Barcelona's extensive junior team network and make joint decisions in what van Gaal described as 'a kind of triumvirate'.
"For the media the short term is important ... but for me the long term is important," said the Dutchman.
Van Gaal said he had been surprised to see the lack of professionalism in the Barcelona organisation.

The Ajax side that van Gaal took to consecutive European Cup finals is known to be supported by one of the most organised structures in soccer, and the club has become a breeding ground for some of the continent's best players.
Van Gaal said he had been approached by Barcelona several years ago, but had to decided to stay on for a season in Amsterdam because of his daughters.
"Barcelona is a great city, but the club is even better. And with the great squad, I hope to continue with the success achieved at Ajax," said van Gaal.
Van Gaal said he would like to keep Ronaldo, the star Brazilian striker whose possible transfer to Inter Milan is currently in the hands of FIFA.
"I'd like to continue with Ronaldo," said Van Gaal.
"If Ronaldo goes, I'll have to find somebody who fits into the team."
Van Gaal also expressed his admiration for fellow Dutchman Johan Cruyff, whose eight years as coach at the club ended acrimoniously last May.
At that stage Barcelona rushed through the signing of Bobby Robson from Portugal's Porto.
As if to show he had learned from one of Robson's biggest problems with Barcelona fans and local media, van Gaal promised to learn Spanish quickly.
The former England manager was also present at the press conference.
"My first wish, not obligation, is to wish van Gaal and his team success -- they understand that word in Holland," said Robson.
"I can tell you that Louis van Gaal will get 100 per cent of support, loyaly, and honesty, and that if there is anything I can do to make his job easier, then he can rely on me."
In his only season in charge Robson had lost favour with Barcelona fans as the league title slipped away to arch-rivals Real Madrid.
But he did take the Spanish Super Cup and the European Cup Winner's Cup before rounding off with Saturday's memorable Spanish Cup victory.
"When I think that my last game with Barcelona as coach is to win the Spanish Cup, it is the most perfect finish," he said.
Ironically the favourite to fill the third key post in the new Barcelona structure is Lorenzo Serra Ferrer, manager of beaten Cup finalists Real Betis.
